I'm glad my visa was extended.
The company sports day was fun.
I'm excited because I have tomorrow off.
Listening to music makes me excited.
I'm excited because a long holiday starts tomorrow.
I'm happy because I'm with my family.
I'm happy that I built a house for my family.
It's fun to hang out with friends.
It was fun to go to a karaoke room with my Korean co-workers.
Long time no see. I'm really glad to see you.
I was really glad to meet someone from my hometown.
tp: 영어 "fun"은 넓게 쓰지만 한국어는 가립니다. 영화는 "재미있다", 여행과 모임은 "즐겁다", 들뜬 마음은 "신나다"입니다.
In English, "fun" is used widely, but Korean separates it: a movie is "재미있다", a trip or a party is "즐겁다", excitement is "신나다".
"기쁘다"는 "기뻐요", "즐겁다"는 "즐거워요"로 바뀝니다.
"기쁘다" becomes "기뻐요", and "즐겁다" becomes "즐거워요".
사람을 만나 좋을 때는 "기쁘다"보다 "반갑다"를 씁니다.
When you are glad to meet someone, use "반갑다" rather than "기쁘다".
dl: 샘 씨, 좋은 일 있어요? 신나 보여요.
Sam, did something good happen? You look excited.
saem ssi, jo-eun il isseoyo? sinna boyeoyo
네, 한국어 시험에 합격했어요. 정말 기뻐요.
Yes, I passed the Korean exam. I'm really glad.
ne, han-gugeo siheome hapkyeokaesseoyo jeongmal gippeoyo
Congratulations! Shall we go out together this weekend?
Sounds good. It will be a fun time.
sm: 좋은 일에는 "기쁘다", 하는 동안에는 "즐겁다", 들뜨면 "신나다", 깊은 마음은 "행복하다"입니다.
For good news use "기쁘다", while doing something "즐겁다", when excited "신나다", and for a deep feeling "행복하다".

i: 영어 "hard, difficult, tired"의 구별입니다. 몸이나 마음이 버거우면 "힘들다", 머리로 풀기 힘들면 "어렵다", 쉬고 싶으면 "피곤하다"입니다.
How to tell "hard, difficult, tired" apart. When your body or mind feels heavy, use "힘들다"; when something is hard to figure out, use "어렵다"; when you want to rest, use "피곤하다".
w: Things are very hard these days.
If things are hard, don't keep it to yourself. Get counseling.
to put up with, to hold back
The bank app is in Korean, so it's difficult.
I went to bed late yesterday, so I'm tired.
If you're tired, take a rest.
This machine is easy to use.
이 앱은 영어도 있어서 쓰기 쉬워요.
i aebeun yeongeodo isseoseo sseugi swiwoyo
This app also has English, so it's easy to use.
My bag is heavy, so my shoulder hurts.
Move heavy things with a forklift.
The heat has worn me out.
지쳤을 때는 고향 음식을 먹으면 힘이 나요.
jicheosseul ttaeneun gohyang eumsigeul meogeumyeon himi nayo
When I'm worn out, eating food from home gives me energy.
to come on (몸살이 나다 = to have body aches)
x: 일이 힘들어요 = The work is hard.
몸이 피곤해요 = My body is tired.
이 일은 쉬워요 = This job is easy.
tp: 영어 "tired(tiring)"는 "힘들다"와 "피곤하다" 둘 다 됩니다. 지금 하는 일이 버거우면 "힘들어요", 쉬고 싶은 몸 상태는 "피곤해요"입니다.
English "tired / tiring" can be both "힘들다" and "피곤하다". If the work you are doing now is hard, say "힘들어요"; if your body wants to rest, say "피곤해요".
"무겁다"는 물건의 무게이고, "힘들다"는 그 일을 하기가 버겁다는 뜻입니다. "상자가 무거워서 힘들어요."
"무겁다" is about how heavy a thing is; "힘들다" means doing it is hard: "상자가 무거워서 힘들어요."
dl: Sam, how is the work going?
일은 어렵지 않은데 서서 하니까 좀 힘듭니다.
The work isn't difficult, but I stand while I work, so it's a bit hard.
ireun eoryeopji aneunde seoseo hanikka jom himdeumnida
처음에는 다 그래요. 피곤하면 쉬는 시간에 꼭 쉬어요.
Everyone feels that way at first. If you're tired, be sure to rest during breaks.
cheo-eumeneun da geuraeyo pigonhamyeon swineun sigane kkok swieoyo
sm: 버거우면 "힘들다", 머리로 풀기 힘들면 "어렵다", 쉬고 싶으면 "피곤하다"입니다.
If it's heavy going, use "힘들다"; if it's hard to work out, "어렵다"; if you want to rest, "피곤하다".

i: 영어 "scared, worried, surprised"의 구별입니다.
How to tell "scared, worried, surprised" apart.
w: At first, I was scared of forklifts.
I'm worried about my parents' health.
I'm worried about my test results.
A typhoon hit my hometown, so I'm worried about my family.
My mother worries about my health.
My mother worries about whether I eat well.
I was startled by a loud noise.
I was surprised when I watched the news.
I was surprised that winter was so cold.
It's my first day at work, so I'm nervous.
I'm nervous because of the job interview.
It's the day of my Korean exam, so I'm nervous.
I feel uneasy when I'm alone.
My visa has run out, so I'm anxious.
My pay hasn't come in, so I'm anxious.
x: 개가 무서워요 = I'm scared of dogs.
시험이 걱정돼요 = I'm worried about the exam.
면접이라서 긴장돼요 = I'm nervous because of the interview.
이 기계는 위험해요 = This machine is dangerous.
tp: 영어 "afraid"는 걱정의 뜻(I'm afraid it will rain)으로도 쓰지만 한국어는 "비가 올까 봐 걱정돼요"라고 합니다. "무섭다"는 정말 겁이 날 때만 씁니다.
In English, "afraid" can also mean worried ("I'm afraid it will rain"), but Korean says "비가 올까 봐 걱정돼요". Use "무섭다" only when you are really scared.
"무섭다"는 "무서워요", "놀라다"는 "놀랐어요"로 씁니다. 놀란 것은 이미 일어난 일이라서 "-았/었-"을 씁니다.
"무섭다" becomes "무서워요", and "놀라다" becomes "놀랐어요". Being surprised has already happened, so use "-았/었-".
일터에서 무섭거나 위험하다고 느끼면 말합니다. "이 작업은 위험해 보입니다. 무섭습니다."
At work, if you feel scared or in danger, say so: "이 작업은 위험해 보입니다. 무섭습니다."
dl: I have a job interview tomorrow, so I'm very nervous.
걱정하지 마세요. 샘 씨는 잘할 거예요.
Don't worry. Sam, you'll do well.
to do well, to be good at
geokjeonghaji maseyo saem ssineun jalhal kkeoyeyo
I'm worried that I won't understand Korean.
그럴 때는 다시 말해 달라고 하면 돼요.
Then you can ask them to say it again.
to ask (-아/어 달라고 = ask someone to)
geureol ttaeneun dasi malhae dallago hamyeon dwaeyo
sm: 겁이 나면 "무섭다", 마음이 놓이지 않으면 "걱정되다", 갑자기는 "놀라다"입니다.
When frightened use "무섭다", when you can't relax "걱정되다", and when something is sudden "놀라다".

i: "괜찮아요"는 영어 "It's okay"처럼 여러 뜻으로 씁니다. 좋다, 필요 없다, 다치지 않았다, 해도 된다는 뜻이 있습니다.
"괜찮아요" has many meanings, much like "It's okay" in English: it's fine, no thanks, I'm not hurt, and you may do it.
w: It's okay to be a little late.
I'm okay. It's just a little scratch.
Would you like some coffee? No, thanks.
Are you okay? Did you get hurt anywhere?
You don't look well. Are you okay?
You're coughing a lot. Are you okay?
The things at this shop are pretty good.
The food at this restaurant tastes pretty good.
This phone plan is cheap and pretty good.
It's okay. I can do it alone.
tp: 사양할 때의 "괜찮아요"는 "No, thanks"입니다. 음식을 더 받고 싶으면 "네, 주세요"라고 말해야 합니다.
When you refuse something, "괜찮아요" means "No, thanks." If you want more food, you must say "네, 주세요".
다쳤거나 아픈데 "괜찮아요"라고 하지 않습니다. 일터에서는 아프면 "안 괜찮습니다. 여기가 아픕니다"라고 바로 말합니다.
Don't say "괜찮아요" when you are hurt or sick. At work, if you are in pain, say right away: "안 괜찮습니다. 여기가 아픕니다".
dl: Oh, sorry! I stepped on your foot. Are you okay?
정말 미안해요. 커피 한 잔 살까요?
I'm really sorry. Can I buy you a cup of coffee?
jeongmal mianhaeyo keopi han jan salkkayo?
No, that's okay. I just had some.
sm: "괜찮아요"는 It's okay, No thanks, Not bad의 뜻으로 씁니다.
"괜찮아요" is used to mean "it's okay", "no, thanks" and "not bad".
qz: "더 드릴까요?" "괜찮아요."의 뜻은? Yes, please / No, thanks
아픈데 일터에서 해야 하는 말은? 괜찮아요 / 여기가 아픕니다

i: "좋다·좋아하다"와 같은 짝입니다. "싫다"는 "이/가", "싫어하다"는 "을/를"을 씁니다. 영어 "dislike, hate"입니다.
It is a pair just like "좋다·좋아하다". "싫다" uses "이/가", and "싫어하다" uses "을/를". They mean "dislike, hate".
w: I don't like night shifts, but the extra pay is good.
My younger brother doesn't like vegetables.
The team leader hates lateness the most.
I don't really like company dinners.
I don't want to do anything today.
It's cold, so I don't want to get up in the morning.
This restaurant is expensive, but the food is not great.
x: 매운 게 싫어요 = I don't like spicy things.
매운 걸 싫어해요 = I don't like spicy things.
매운 걸 안 좋아해요 = I don't really like spicy things.
가기 싫어요 = I don't want to go.
tp: "싫어요"는 아주 센 말입니다. 권하는 것을 거절할 때 "싫어요"라고 하면 실례입니다. "괜찮습니다"나 "별로 안 좋아해요"를 씁니다.
"싫어요" is a very strong word. It is rude to say "싫어요" when you refuse an offer. Use "괜찮습니다" or "별로 안 좋아해요".
그러나 싫은 접촉이나 괴롭힘에는 또렷하게 "싫어요", "하지 마세요"라고 말합니다.
But against unwanted touching or harassment, say clearly: "싫어요", "하지 마세요".
dl: Sam, will you have a drink at the company dinner?
죄송합니다. 저는 술을 별로 안 좋아합니다.
I'm sorry. I don't really like alcohol.
joesonghamnida jeoneun sureul byeollo an joahamnida
Really? Then have a soft drink.
sm: "이/가 싫다", "을/를 싫어하다"이고, 부드럽게는 "별로 안 좋아해요"입니다.
It is "이/가 싫다" and "을/를 싫어하다", and the soft way is "별로 안 좋아해요".
qz: 부드럽게 거절하는 말은? 싫어요 / 별로 안 좋아해요

i: 모두 영어 "very, really"와 가깝습니다. 세기와 말씨가 조금씩 다릅니다.
All of them are close to "very, really" in English. They differ a little in strength and style.
w: to do well, to be good at
This month's results are very good.
공장 안이 너무 더워서 머리가 아파요.
gongjang ani neomu deowoseo meoriga apayo
It's too hot inside the factory, so I have a headache.
to eat, to take (honorific of 먹다)
We're getting a lot of orders these days.
This chemical is very dangerous, so be careful.
x: too much; in speech it can also mean "very"
tp: 영어 "very"처럼 한국어도 꾸미는 말 앞에 옵니다. "very expensive"는 "아주 비싸요"입니다.
Like "very" in English, Korean puts it before the word: "very expensive" is "아주 비싸요".
"많이"는 동사와 쓰고(많이 먹어요), "아주"는 형용사와 씁니다(아주 커요). "아주 먹어요"는 틀립니다.
"많이" goes with verbs (많이 먹어요), and "아주" goes with adjectives (아주 커요). "아주 먹어요" is wrong.
윗사람에게는 "진짜"보다 "정말"이 점잖습니다.
With older people or bosses, "정말" is more polite than "진짜".
dl: The kimchi stew at this restaurant is really delicious.
It really is. But it's too spicy for me.
Really? Drink a lot of water.
sm: 점잖게는 "아주", 지나치면 "너무", 참말이면 "정말, 진짜", 양은 "많이"입니다.
"아주" is polite, "너무" is too much, "정말, 진짜" mean truly, and "많이" is for amount.
qz: 윗사람에게 더 점잖은 말은? 진짜 / 정말

i: 모두 영어 "a little"입니다. "좀"은 "조금"의 준말이지만 부탁을 부드럽게 하는 말로도 씁니다.
All of them mean "a little". "좀" is short for "조금", but it is also used to make a request softer.
w: I can speak a little Korean.
We finish a little early today.
Could you open the window, please?
Just a little more and you're done. Hang in there.
to cheer up, to hang in there
My Korean is getting better little by little.
Add the water little by little.
I'm saving a little from my pay each month.
x: 조금 매워요 = It's a little spicy.
좀 비싸요 = It's a bit expensive.
조금만 주세요 = Just a little, please.
tp: 부탁의 "좀"은 양의 뜻이 없습니다. "이것 좀 보세요"는 "조금만 보세요"가 아니라 "Please look at this"입니다.
"좀" in a request has no meaning of amount. "이것 좀 보세요" does not mean "look a little"; it means "Please look at this."
한국 사람은 나쁜 말을 "좀"으로 부드럽게 합니다. "좀 비싸네요"는 사실 "It's expensive"라는 뜻이고, "좀 어렵겠는데요"는 "No, I can't"라는 뜻일 때가 많습니다.
Koreans use "좀" to soften bad news. "좀 비싸네요" really means "It's expensive," and "좀 어렵겠는데요" often means "No, I can't."
dl: to do well, to be good at
Not at all. I can only speak a little.
Could you take a look at this document?
Sure. But it's a bit difficult for me.
sm: 양은 "조금, 약간", 부탁을 부드럽게 할 때는 "좀"입니다.
For amount use "조금, 약간"; to make a request softer use "좀".
qz: 물 (   ) 주세요. (Some water, please.) 좀 / 약간

i: 얼마나 자주 하는지를 나타내는 말입니다. 영어처럼 동사 앞에 옵니다.
Words that say how often you do something. Like in English, they come before the verb.
w: The team leader always comes early.
Always carry your residence card with you.
to have, to bring (가지고 오다 = to bring)
I usually get up at seven.
On weekends, I usually rest at home.
On Sundays, I usually go grocery shopping.
market (장을 보다 = to go grocery shopping)
I often come to this restaurant.
가끔 고향 친구들과 영상 통화를 해요.
gakkeum gohyang chin-gudeulgwa yeongsang tonghwareul haeyo
Sometimes I video call my friends back home.
I don't drink alcohol at all.
I don't know Korean at all.
At first, I couldn't speak Korean at all.
can't do, to be bad at
매일 아침 체조를 하고 일을 시작해요.
mae-il achim chejoreul hago ireul sijakaeyo
Every morning, we do stretching exercises and then start work.
tp: "전혀, 별로, 절대"는 반드시 "안, 못, 없다"와 같이 씁니다. "전혀 마셔요"는 틀립니다.
"전혀, 별로, 절대" must always go with "안, 못, 없다". "전혀 마셔요" is wrong.
자리: "I often call my parents"는 "부모님께 자주 전화해요"로, "자주"가 동사 앞에 옵니다.
Position: "I often call my parents" is "부모님께 자주 전화해요". "자주" comes before the verb.
"자주"(often)와 "자꾸"(again and again, for bad things)를 가립니다. "자꾸 잊어버려요."
Tell "자주" (often) and "자꾸" (again and again, for bad things) apart: "자꾸 잊어버려요."
dl: 샘 씨는 주말에 보통 뭐 해요?
Sam, what do you usually do on weekends?
saem ssineun jumare botong mwo haeyo?
보통 기숙사에서 쉬어요. 가끔 친구들하고 축구를 해요.
I usually rest in the dormitory. Sometimes I play soccer with my friends.
botong gisuksa-eseo swieoyo gakkeum chin-gudeulhago chukkureul haeyo
sm: 항상 → 보통 → 자주 → 가끔 → 전혀 안.
항상 → 보통 → 자주 → 가끔 → 전혀 안.

i: 영어 "already"와 "yet, still"의 구별입니다. 생각보다 빠르면 "벌써", 끝난 일이면 "이미", 끝나지 않았으면 "아직"입니다.
How to tell "already" and "yet / still" apart. If it is sooner than you thought, use "벌써"; if it is already finished, "이미"; if it isn't finished, "아직".
w: The application period has already ended.
There's still a long way to go.
My pay hasn't come in yet.
Do you still work at that company?
Now I'm used to taking the subway.
x: 아직 안 끝났어요 = It isn't finished yet.
tp: "다 했어요?"에 "Not yet"이라고 대답하려면 "아직이요" 또는 "아직 안 했어요"라고 합니다.
To answer "Not yet" to "다 했어요?", say "아직이요" or "아직 안 했어요".
"아직 안 했어요"는 "I haven't done it yet"이고, "아직 안 해요"는 "I'm not doing it"에 가깝습니다. 보통 "-았/었-"을 씁니다.
"아직 안 했어요" means "I haven't done it yet," and "아직 안 해요" is closer to "I'm not doing it." Usually use "-았/었-".
dl: 아직 다 못 했습니다. 십 분만 더 주십시오.
I'm not done yet. Please give me just ten more minutes.
ajik da mot haetseumnida sip bunman deo jusipsio
sm: 빠르면 "벌써", 끝난 일은 "이미", 안 끝났으면 "아직"입니다.
If it's fast, "벌써"; if it's finished, "이미"; if it's not finished, "아직".

i: 지금과 가까운 때를 나타내는 말입니다. 조금 전인지 조금 뒤인지를 가립니다.
Words for a time close to now. They show whether it was a moment ago or will be in a moment.
w: I just got a delivery text.
The team leader was looking for you earlier.
Let's talk later during the break.
Let's have a meal together sometime.
돈을 모아서 나중에 가게를 하고 싶어요.
doneul moaseo najunge gagereul hago sipeoyo
I want to save money and open a shop later.
x: 조금 전, 조금 뒤 둘 다
tp: "이따가"는 오늘 안의 일이고, "나중에"는 언제인지 정해지지 않은 뒷날입니다.
"이따가" is for later today, and "나중에" is for some later day that isn't fixed.
"방금"은 지난 일에만 씁니다. "방금 갈게요"는 틀리고 "금방 갈게요"가 맞습니다.
"방금" is used only for the past. "방금 갈게요" is wrong; "금방 갈게요" is right.
한국 사람의 "금방"은 꽤 빠릅니다. "금방 갈게요"라고 했으면 서두릅니다.
When Koreans say "금방", it is quite fast. If you said "금방 갈게요", hurry.
dl: Sam, have you seen the manager?
방금 창고로 가셨습니다. 곧 오실 겁니다.
He just went to the warehouse. He'll be back soon.
banggeum changgoro gasyeotseumnida got osil geomnida
Really? Then I'll come back later.
sm: 조금 전은 "방금, 아까", 조금 뒤는 "곧, 이따가", 빨리는 "금방"입니다.
A moment ago is "방금, 아까", a little later is "곧, 이따가", and quickly is "금방".
qz: 맞는 것은? 방금 갈게요 / 금방 갈게요

i: 영어 "fast"와 "early"처럼 한국어도 둘로 가립니다. 움직임이 빠르면 "빨리", 때가 이르면 "일찍"입니다.
Like "fast" and "early" in English, Korean has two different words. For fast movement use "빨리"; for an early time use "일찍".
w: 다친 사람이 있어요. 빨리 와 주세요!
dachin sarami isseoyo ppalli wa juseyo
Someone is hurt. Please come quickly!
Go to bed early so you won't be tired tomorrow.
It's okay to go slowly, so do it correctly.
I went to bed late yesterday.
If you finish work late, the dormitory cafeteria is closed.
늦을 것 같으면 반장님께 문자 보내세요.
neujeul geot gateumyeon banjangnimkke munja bonaeseyo
If you think you'll be late, text the team leader.
The subway is faster than the bus.
Deliveries in Korea are really fast.
x: 일찍 일어나요 = I get up early.
늦게 자요 = I go to bed late.
tp: 영어 "slowly"와 "late"처럼 한국어도 둘로 가립니다. 움직임이 느리면 "천천히", 때가 늦으면 "늦게"입니다.
The same goes for "slowly" and "late". For slow movement use "천천히"; for a late time use "늦게".
"빨리 일어나세요"는 지금 얼른 일어나라는 뜻이고, "일찍 일어나세요"는 이른 시간에 일어나라는 뜻입니다.
"빨리 일어나세요" means get up quickly right now, and "일찍 일어나세요" means get up at an early time.
한국 일터에서는 "빨리빨리"를 자주 듣습니다. 그러나 안전이 먼저입니다. "천천히 정확하게 하겠습니다."
At Korean workplaces you often hear "빨리빨리". But safety comes first: "천천히 정확하게 하겠습니다."
dl: 내일은 물량이 많으니까 삼십 분 일찍 나와요.
We have a lot of stock tomorrow, so come in thirty minutes early.
nae-ireun mullyangi maneunikka samsip bun iljjik nawayo
Okay, I'll be here by seven thirty.
그리고 이 상자들 빨리 옮겨요. 트럭이 곧 와요.
And move these boxes quickly. The truck is coming soon.
geurigo i sangjadeul ppalli omkkyeoyo teureogi got wayo
sm: 움직임은 "빨리·천천히", 때는 "일찍·늦게"입니다.
For movement use "빨리·천천히", and for time use "일찍·늦게".
qz: 말이 빨라요. (   ) 말해 주세요. 천천히 / 늦게

i: 둘 다 영어 "again"입니다. "다시"는 처음부터 새로 하는 것이고, "또"는 같은 일이 한 번 더 일어나는 것입니다.
Both mean "again" in English. "다시" means doing something over from the start, and "또" means the same thing happens one more time.
w: Could you say that again, please?
Can I have a little more rice, please?
Please give me one more pair of gloves.
계좌 번호를 한 번 더 확인해 주세요.
gejwa beonhoreul han beon deo hwaginhae juseyo
Please check the account number one more time.
Contact us by phone or text.
Pay in cash or by card.
Please show your passport or residence card.
x: 다시 하세요 = Do it again (from the start).
한 번 더 해요 = Do it one more time.
tp: 못 알아들었을 때는 "다시 한번 말씀해 주세요"입니다. "또 말해 주세요"는 어색합니다.
When you didn't understand, say "다시 한번 말씀해 주세요". "또 말해 주세요" sounds unnatural.
"또"는 꾸짖는 말에 자주 나옵니다. "또 늦었어요?", "또 틀렸네요."
"또" often comes up when someone is scolding: "또 늦었어요?", "또 틀렸네요."
영어 "more"처럼 양을 보태는 뜻이면 "더"입니다. "하나 더 주세요."
When you mean adding more, like "more" in English, use "더": "하나 더 주세요."
dl: 이 상자는 테이프가 잘못 붙었어요. 다시 포장해요.
The tape on this box is stuck on wrong. Pack it again.
i sangjaneun te-ipeuga jalmot buteosseoyo dasi pojanghaeyo
I'm sorry. I'll do it again.
또 틀리면 안 돼요. 한 번 더 확인하고요.
You can't get it wrong again. Check it one more time, too.
tto teullimyeon an dwaeyo han beon deo hwaginhagoyo
sm: 새로 하면 "다시", 거듭되면 "또", 보태면 "더"입니다.
For doing over use "다시", for repeating "또", and for adding "더".
qz: 못 알아들었습니다. (   ) 한번 말씀해 주세요. 다시 / 또

i: 모두 영어 "all"입니다. "다"는 말에서 가장 많이 쓰고 "남김없이 끝까지"라는 뜻도 있습니다.
All of them mean "all". "다" is the most common in speech, and it also means "completely, to the end".
w: How many people are there in total?
Everyone, gather near the emergency exit.
How much is all my shopping in total?
market (장 보다 = to shop for groceries)
I didn't understand anything in the class.
x: 다 했어요 = I've done it all.
전부 얼마예요? = How much is it in total?
다들 어디 갔어요? = Where did everyone go?
거의 다 했어요 = I'm almost done.
tp: "다 했어요?"는 일터에서 가장 자주 듣는 물음입니다. "네, 다 했습니다", "거의 다 했습니다", "아직 못 했습니다"로 대답합니다.
"다 했어요?" is the question you hear most often at work. Answer "네, 다 했습니다", "거의 다 했습니다", or "아직 못 했습니다".
"모두"와 "전부"는 명사처럼도 씁니다. "모두가 알아요", "전부를 주세요". "다"는 그렇게 쓰지 않습니다.
"모두" and "전부" can also be used like nouns: "모두가 알아요", "전부를 주세요". "다" is not used that way.
dl: 네, 모두 왔습니다. 전부 여덟 명입니다.
Yes, everyone is here. There are eight people in total.
ne, modu watseumnida jeonbu yeodeol myeongimnida
Is all the morning work finished?
거의 다 했습니다. 상자 두 개만 남았습니다.
Almost done. Only two boxes are left.
geo-i da haetseumnida sangja du gaeman namatseumnida
sm: 끝까지는 "다", 사람과 물건 전체는 "모두", 셈은 "전부"입니다.
For "to the end" use "다", for all people or things "모두", and for counting a total "전부".
qz: "How much is it in total?"를 한국어로?

i: 문장과 문장을 잇는 말입니다. "그리고"는 보태는 말(and, and then)이고 "그래서"는 까닭과 결과를 잇는 말(so, that's why)입니다.
Words that link one sentence to another. "그리고" adds something (and, and then), and "그래서" links a reason and a result (so, that's why).
w: 저는 샘이에요. 그리고 이 사람은 아이샤예요.
jeoneun saemieyo geurigo i sarameun a-isyayeyo
I'm Sam. And this is Aisha.
I ate. And then I had coffee.
마트에서 쌀을 샀어요. 그리고 고추도 샀어요.
mateu-eseo ssareul sasseoyo geurigo gochudo sasseoyo
I bought rice at the supermarket. And I bought chili peppers too.
어제 아팠어요. 그래서 회사에 못 갔어요.
eoje apasseoyo geuraeseo hoesa-e mot gasseoyo
I was sick yesterday. So I couldn't go to work.
It rained. So I stayed home.
I missed the bus. So I took a taxi.
Turn off the power. After that, clean it.
Wash your hands. Then put on gloves.
First take a number ticket. Then wait.
And then? What did the boss say?
And then? Did you go to the hospital?
I did my homework. After that, I went to bed.
I took a shower. After that, I ate.
Work finished. After that, I took a shower.
tp: 한 문장으로 이으면 "그리고"는 "-고", "그래서"는 "-아서/어서"가 됩니다. "비가 와서 안 가요."
When you join them into one sentence, "그리고" becomes "-고", and "그래서" becomes "-아서/어서": "비가 와서 안 가요."
낱말과 낱말을 이을 때는 "그리고"보다 "하고"를 씁니다. "빵하고 우유".
To join two words, use "하고" rather than "그리고": "빵하고 우유".
dl: 샘 씨, 어제 왜 일찍 갔어요?
Sam, why did you leave early yesterday?
saem ssi, eoje wae iljjik gasseoyo?
머리가 많이 아팠습니다. 그래서 병원에 갔습니다.
I had a bad headache. So I went to the hospital.
meoriga mani apatseumnida geuraeseo byeongwone gatseumnida
네, 약을 먹었습니다. 그리고 푹 잤습니다.
Yes, I took medicine. And I slept well.
ne, yageul meogeotseumnida geurigo puk jatseumnida
sm: 보탤 때는 "그리고", 결과를 말할 때는 "그래서"입니다.
Use "그리고" to add something and "그래서" to say a result.
qz: 비가 와요. (   ) 우산을 써요. 그리고 / 그래서
저는 샘이에요. (   ) 미국 사람이에요. 그리고 / 그래서

i: 모두 영어 "but"입니다. "그런데"는 말머리를 돌릴 때(by the way)도 씁니다.
All of them mean "but". "그런데" is also used to change the topic (by the way).
w: Korean is difficult. But it's fun.
Korea is cold. But the snow is pretty.
There's a lot of work. But it's okay.
The pay is low. But the dormitory is free.
By the way, what time is it now?
By the way, who is that person?
By the way, is next week's work schedule out?
to come out, to come in (to work)
By the way, where are you going?
By the way, did you eat?
By the way, are you off tomorrow?
I'm tired. But I still have to go.
It's raining. But I'm still going.
힘들어요. 그래도 가족을 생각하면 힘이 나요.
himdeureoyo geuraedo gajogeul saenggakamyeon himi nayo
It's hard. Still, when I think of my family, I feel stronger.
to come on (몸살이 나다 = to have body aches)
tp: 한 문장으로 이으면 "-지만"이나 "-는데"가 됩니다. "비싸지만 맛있어요."
When you join them into one sentence, they become "-지만" or "-는데": "비싸지만 맛있어요."
"그런데"로 말을 시작하면 새 이야기를 꺼낸다는 신호입니다. "그런데요, 반장님…"
Starting with "그런데" is a sign that you are bringing up something new: "그런데요, 반장님…"
윗사람의 말에 "하지만"으로 바로 받으면 대드는 것처럼 들릴 수 있습니다. "네, 그런데요…"로 부드럽게 시작합니다.
If you answer an older person or boss right away with "하지만", it can sound like you are arguing. Start softly with "네, 그런데요…".
dl: The room is small. But it's clean.
That's good. By the way, have you had dinner?
Not yet. Shall we eat together?
sm: 반대는 "하지만, 그렇지만", 말머리를 돌릴 때는 "그런데"입니다.
For a contrast use "하지만, 그렇지만", and to change the topic use "그런데".

i: 영어 "then, in that case"입니다. "그럼"은 "그러면"의 준말인데, "of course"라는 대답으로도 씁니다.
It means "then, in that case". "그럼" is short for "그러면", but it is also used as an answer meaning "of course".
w: Then I'll come back tomorrow morning.
Well then, I'll be going now.
(먼저 가 보겠습니다 = I'll be leaving first)
Then I'll contact you again next week.
Can I go with you? Of course.
Of course. Ask me any time.
Can I go first? Yes, go ahead.
Can I leave work first? Yes, go ahead.
Oh, so that's how they do it in Korea. I see.
tp: 헤어질 때 "그럼"으로 말을 시작합니다. "그럼, 안녕히 계세요", "그럼 들어가세요".
When saying goodbye, start with "그럼": "그럼, 안녕히 계세요", "그럼 들어가세요".
"그럼요"는 흔쾌히 "네"라고 하는 대답입니다. 윗사람에게는 "네, 물론입니다"가 더 점잖습니다.
"그럼요" is a happy "yes". With older people or bosses, "네, 물론입니다" is more polite.
한 문장으로 이으면 "-(으)면"입니다. "시간이 없으면 내일 하세요."
When you join it into one sentence, it becomes "-(으)면": "시간이 없으면 내일 하세요."
dl: Team leader, we've run out of materials today.
그래요? 그럼 오늘은 청소하고 일찍 끝냅시다.
Really? Then let's clean up and finish early today.
geuraeyo? geureom oneureun cheongsohago iljjik kkeunnaepsida
Should I come in at the usual time tomorrow?
sm: "그럼"은 then, "그럼요"는 of course입니다.
"그럼" means "then", and "그럼요" means "of course".

i: "그러니까"는 까닭을 먼저 말하고 결과를 잇는 말(so)이고, "왜냐하면"은 결과를 먼저 말하고 까닭을 대는 말(because)입니다.
"그러니까" gives the reason first and then the result (so), and "왜냐하면" gives the result first and then the reason (because).
w: We don't have time. So hurry up.
It's raining. So take an umbrella.
내일 비가 온대요. 그러니까 우산 챙기세요.
nae-il biga ondaeyo geureonikka usan chaenggiseyo
They say it will rain tomorrow. So bring an umbrella.
오늘은 못 가요. 왜냐하면 야간 근무가 있거든요.
oneureun mot gayo waenyahamyeon yagan geunmuga itkeodeunyo
I can't go today. Because I have a night shift.
한국에 왔어요. 왜냐하면 돈을 벌고 싶었거든요.
han-guge wasseoyo waenyahamyeon doneul beolgo sipeotkeodeunyo
I came to Korea. Because I wanted to earn money.
다음 달에 휴가를 써요. 왜냐하면 동생이 결혼하거든요.
da-eum dare hyugareul sseoyo waenyahamyeon dongsaengi gyeolhonhageodeunyo
I'm taking time off next month. Because my younger brother is getting married.
I was late because of the rain.
눈 때문에 통근 버스가 안 와요.
nun ttaemune tonggeun beoseuga an wayo
The shuttle bus isn't coming because of the snow.
Thanks to you, it ended well.
I passed the exam thanks to my professor.
동료들 덕분에 한국 생활에 빨리 적응했어요.
dongnyodeul deokpune han-guk saenghware ppalli jeogeunghaesseoyo
Thanks to my co-workers, I got used to life in Korea quickly.
to adjust, to get used to
It's so hot, isn't it? I know, right?
I know. Prices have gone up so much these days.
tp: 시키는 말과 권하는 말 앞에는 "그래서"가 아니라 "그러니까"를 씁니다.
Before an order or a suggestion, use "그러니까", not "그래서".
"때문에"는 나쁜 결과에, "덕분에"는 좋은 결과에 씁니다. "반장님 덕분에 잘 배웠습니다."
"때문에" is for bad results, and "덕분에" is for good results: "반장님 덕분에 잘 배웠습니다."
dl: 이 기계는 날이 날카로워요. 그러니까 꼭 장갑을 껴요.
The blade on this machine is sharp. So be sure to wear gloves.
i gigeneun nari nalkarowoyo geureonikka kkok janggabeul kkyeoyo
네. 그런데 왜 전원을 먼저 끕니까?
Okay. But why do we turn off the power first?
ne geureonde wae jeonwoneul meonjeo kkeumnikka?
I understand. Thanks to you, I'm learning a lot.
sm: 결과를 이을 때는 "그러니까", 까닭을 댈 때는 "왜냐하면"입니다.
To give the result use "그러니까", and to give the reason use "왜냐하면".
qz: 좋은 결과의 까닭에 쓰는 말은? 때문에 / 덕분에
못 가요. (   ) 일이 있어요. 그러니까 / 왜냐하면

i: 영어 "what, which, what kind of"에 해당하는 물음말입니다. 혼자 쓰는 말과 명사 앞에 쓰는 말을 가립니다.
Question words for "what, which, what kind of". Some are used alone, and some come before a noun.
w: What do you want to eat?
What's on the lunch menu today?
What kind of food do you like?
What kind of work have you done?
Which bank has cheap fees for sending money abroad?
Excuse me. What did you say?
Sorry, what? Please say it again.
뭐라고요? 기계 소리 때문에 안 들려요.
mworagoyo? gige sori ttaemune an deullyeoyo
What? I can't hear you because of the machine noise.
x: 뭐 해요? = What are you doing?
무슨 일을 해요? = What work do you do?
어떤 사람이에요? = What kind of person is he?
어느 나라 사람이에요? = Which country are you from?
tp: 물음말의 자리가 영어와 다릅니다. 영어는 "What are you doing?"처럼 물음말이 맨 앞에 오지만, 한국어는 "뭐 해요?"처럼 동사 앞에 옵니다.
The place of the question word is different from English. English puts it first ("What are you doing?"), but Korean puts it before the verb: "뭐 해요?"
"뭐"는 "무엇"의 준말입니다. 말할 때는 "뭐", 글이나 격식 있는 말에서는 "무엇"을 씁니다.
"뭐" is short for "무엇". Use "뭐" when speaking, and "무엇" in writing or formal speech.
"무슨 일 있어요?"는 "Is something wrong?"라는 걱정의 말입니다.
"무슨 일 있어요?" is a caring question: "Is something wrong?"
dl: What work did you do in Greece?
I worked at a car repair shop.
sm: 혼자는 "뭐", 종류는 "무슨", 성질은 "어떤", 고를 때는 "어느"입니다.
Use "뭐" alone, "무슨" for type, "어떤" for what something is like, and "어느" for choosing.

i: 영어 "how many, how much, how long"의 구별입니다. 셀 수 있으면 "몇", 값은 "얼마", 시간이나 정도는 "얼마나"입니다.
How to tell "how many, how much, how long" apart. For things you can count use "몇", for prices "얼마", and for time or degree "얼마나".
w: How many apples did you buy?
How many do we have to make today?
How many people are there in total?
How many people are in your family?
How many people are coming from Myanmar this time?
What time does the shuttle bus come?
How much is the dormitory fee per month?
How long does it take from here?
How long have you been in Korea?
How long does a visa extension take?
How many days are you off?
How many days were you in Korea?
How many days is the summer vacation?
x: 몇 개예요? = How many are there?
얼마나 걸려요? = How long does it take?
오늘이 며칠이에요? = What's the date today?
tp: "몇" 뒤에는 꼭 세는 말이 옵니다. 몇 개, 몇 명, 몇 시, 몇 살, 몇 번, 몇 층.
"몇" must always be followed by a counter: 몇 개, 몇 명, 몇 시, 몇 살, 몇 번, 몇 층.
"몇 일"이라고 쓰지 않고 "며칠"이라고 씁니다. "몇 월 며칠이에요?"
Don't write "몇 일"; write "며칠": "몇 월 며칠이에요?"
"몇"의 소리는 뒤의 말에 따라 달라집니다. 몇 명 [면 명], 몇 개 [멷 깨], 몇 월 [며 둴].
The sound of "몇" changes with the next word: 몇 명 [면 명], 몇 개 [멷 깨], 몇 월 [며 둴].
dl: It's 1,500 won. How many would you like?
다섯 개 주세요. 여기에서 시청까지 얼마나 걸려요?
Five, please. How long does it take from here to City Hall?
daseot gae juseyo yeogieseo sicheongkkaji eolmana geollyeoyo?
It takes about ten minutes on foot.
sm: 수는 "몇", 값은 "얼마", 시간과 정도는 "얼마나"입니다.
For numbers use "몇", for prices "얼마", and for time and degree "얼마나".

i: 때, 곳, 사람을 묻는 말입니다. 영어 "when, where, who"입니다. 조사가 붙으면 모양이 조금 달라집니다.
Questions about time, place and people: "when, where, who". Their form changes a little when a particle is added.
w: When did you come to Korea?
When does your employment contract end?
Where is the nearest counseling center for foreigners?
Who is in charge of the dormitory?
By when do I have to do it?
Until when will you be in Korea?
By when do I have to hand in the documents?
Where did you like the most?
x: 언제 와요? = When are you coming?
tp: "누구가"가 아니라 "누가"입니다. "누가 왔어요?"
It is "누가", not "누구가": "누가 왔어요?"
"언제"에는 "에"를 붙이지 않습니다. "언제에 와요?"는 틀립니다. "어디"에는 붙입니다. "어디에 가요?"
Don't add "에" to "언제". "언제에 와요?" is wrong. You can add it to "어디": "어디에 가요?"
pr: 어디에서 (where you do something, where from)
dl: Excuse me. Where is Manager Kim?
He's in a meeting now. Who are you?
I'm Sam from the production department. When does the meeting end?
It will end around three o'clock.
sm: 때는 "언제", 곳은 "어디", 사람은 "누구"이고 "누구 + 가"는 "누가"입니다.
For time use "언제", for place "어디", for people "누구", and "누구 + 가" is "누가".
qz: 맞는 것은? 누구가 왔어요? / 누가 왔어요?
맞는 것은? 언제에 와요? / 언제 와요?

i: 까닭, 방법, 느낌을 묻는 말입니다. 영어 "why, how, how is it"입니다.
Questions about reasons, ways and feelings: "why, how, how is it".
w: Why is my pay so low this month?
How do I get to City Hall?
How do I sort the recycling?
I lost my wallet. What should I do?
I lost my residence card. What should I do?
x: 왜 안 와요? = Why isn't he coming?
어떻게 해요? = How do I do it?
맛이 어때요? = How does it taste?
성함이 어떻게 되세요? = May I have your name?
tp: "왜요?"는 말투에 따라 따지는 것처럼 들립니다. 윗사람에게는 "무슨 일이십니까?", "이유를 여쭤봐도 될까요?"가 좋습니다.
"왜요?" can sound like a challenge, depending on your tone. With older people or bosses, "무슨 일이십니까?" or "이유를 여쭤봐도 될까요?" is better.
"어떻게"는 하는 방법을, "어때요"는 느낌이나 생각을 묻습니다. "어떻게 가요?"(how to get there), "거기 어때요?"(Is it nice there?).
"어떻게" asks how to do something, and "어때요" asks about feelings or opinions: "어떻게 가요?" (how to get there), "거기 어때요?" (Is it nice there?).
dl: 통장을 만들고 싶은데 어떻게 하면 돼요?
I'd like to open a bank account. What should I do?
tongjangeul mandeulgo sipeunde eotteoke hamyeon dwaeyo?
이 신청서를 쓰시면 됩니다. 이 통장은 어떠세요?
Just fill out this application form. How about this account?
i sincheongseoreul sseusimyeon doemnida i tongjangeun eotteoseyo?
sm: 까닭은 "왜", 방법은 "어떻게", 느낌은 "어때요"입니다.
For reasons use "왜", for ways "어떻게", and for feelings "어때요".

i: 모두 영어 "work"입니다. 말할 때는 "일", 현장에서는 "작업", 사무실에서는 "업무", 일하는 시간과 자리는 "근무"입니다.
All of them mean "work". In speech use "일", on site "작업", in the office "업무", and for work hours and duty "근무".
w: I have a lot of work today.
What do you do for work?
When work is over, let's have dinner together.
Don't make phone calls while working.
Don't look at your phone while working.
새 업무를 배우는 데 한 달 걸렸어요.
sae eommureul bae-uneun de han dal geollyeosseoyo
It took me a month to learn my new duties.
This week I'm on the night shift.
What was your job back home?
If you work overtime, you get extra pay.
If you don't want to work overtime, you don't have to.
x: 직업이 뭐예요? = What is your job?
tp: 안내판에서 "작업 중"은 "Work in progress, keep away", "근무 중"은 "On duty"입니다.
On signs, "작업 중" means "Work in progress, keep away", and "근무 중" means "On duty".
"일"은 "matter, thing"의 뜻도 있습니다. "무슨 일이에요?"(What's the matter?), "일이 생겼어요"(Something came up).
"일" can also mean "matter, thing": "무슨 일이에요?" (What's the matter?), "일이 생겼어요" (Something came up).
근로계약서에는 "근무 장소, 근무 시간, 업무 내용"이 나옵니다. 꼭 확인합니다.
An employment contract shows "근무 장소, 근무 시간, 업무 내용" (workplace, working hours, job duties). Be sure to check them.
dl: 다음 주부터 샘 씨는 야간 근무예요.
From next week, Sam is on the night shift.
da-eum jubuteo saem ssineun yagan geunmuyeyo
밤 아홉 시부터 아침 여섯 시까지예요. 작업 내용은 같아요.
From nine at night to six in the morning. The work is the same.
bam ahop sibuteo achim yeoseot sikkajiyeyo jageop naeyongeun gatayo
I understand. Is there overtime too?
sm: 말로는 "일", 현장은 "작업", 사무는 "업무", 나와서 일하는 것은 "근무"입니다.
In speech use "일", on site "작업", for office work "업무", and for coming in to work "근무".

i: 일하고 받는 돈을 가리키는 말입니다. 말할 때는 "월급", 서류에는 "급여, 임금", 덧붙는 돈은 "수당"입니다.
Words for the money you get for working. In speech use "월급", in documents "급여, 임금", and for extra money "수당".
w: When I get paid, I send half of it home.
Please give me my pay slip.
My pay went into my bank account.
Open your salary account in your own name.
If you don't get your wages, report it to the labor office.
to be paid, to come out
If you work on a holiday, you get more extra pay.
to come out, to come in (to work)
The hourly wage is higher at night.
아르바이트 시급이 최저 임금보다 적으면 안 돼요.
areuba-iteu sigeubi choejeo imgeumboda jeogeumyeon an dwaeyo
A part-time job's hourly wage must not be lower than the minimum wage.
Check the amount deducted for the dormitory fee.
My take-home pay is more than last month.
If your take-home pay is different from your contract, ask about it.
tp: 급여 명세서는 "지급"(payments)과 "공제"(deductions)로 나뉩니다. 지급에서 공제를 빼면 "실수령액"입니다.
A pay slip is divided into "지급" (payments) and "공제" (deductions). Payments minus deductions is "실수령액" (take-home pay).
월급을 제때 못 받는 것을 "임금 체불"이라고 합니다. 고용노동부 1350에 물어볼 수 있습니다.
Not getting your pay on time is called "임금 체불" (unpaid wages). You can ask the Ministry of Employment and Labor at 1350.
야간(밤 열 시 이후), 연장(하루 여덟 시간 넘게), 휴일에 일하면 수당이 붙습니다.
If you work at night (after 10 p.m.), overtime (more than eight hours a day), or on a holiday, you get extra pay.
dl: 과장님, 이번 달 급여 명세서를 봤는데 질문이 있습니다.
Manager, I looked at this month's pay slip and I have a question.
gwajangnim, ibeon dal geubyeo myeongseseoreul bwanneunde jilmuni itseumnida
My night shift pay is less than last month.
확인해 볼게요. 근무 기록을 같이 봅시다.
I'll check. Let's look at your work records together.
hwaginhae bolgeyo geunmu girogeul gachi bopsida
sm: 말로는 "월급", 서류는 "급여·임금", 덧붙는 돈은 "수당"입니다.
In speech use "월급", in documents "급여·임금", and for extra money "수당".
qz: 월급을 못 받는 것을 무엇이라고 합니까?

i: "휴(休)"는 쉰다는 뜻입니다. 정해진 쉬는 날은 "휴일", 내가 신청해서 쉬는 날은 "휴가", 일하다가 잠깐 쉬는 것은 "휴식"입니다.
"휴(休)" means rest. A fixed day off is "휴일", days off you ask for are "휴가", and a short rest during work is "휴식".
w: What do you do on your day off?
When is your next day off?
Let's go to the beach together on our day off.
This Friday is a public holiday.
휴일에도 농장 동물은 밥을 줘야 해요.
hyu-iredo nongjang dongmureun babeul jwoya haeyo
Even on holidays, the farm animals have to be fed.
I'd like to ask for time off.
I'm going to my hometown during my vacation.
Plane tickets are expensive during the vacation season.
더운 날에는 휴식 시간을 더 줘요.
deo-un nareneun hyusik siganeul deo jwoyo
On hot days, they give more break time.
How many days of annual leave do you have left?
I'm taking annual leave and going to my hometown.
Annual leave is fifteen days a year.
I was sick, so I took sick leave.
How many days of sick leave can I take?
병가를 쓸 때는 병원 영수증을 내세요.
byeonggareul sseul ttaeneun byeongwon yeongsujeungeul naeseyo
When you take sick leave, hand in your hospital receipt.
Take a short rest and then do it.
I had a good rest on the weekend.
If you have a headache, take a short rest and then continue.
x: 연차를 쓰다 = to use annual leave
tp: "휴가를 내다, 휴가를 쓰다, 휴가를 받다"처럼 말합니다. "내일 휴가를 내고 싶습니다."
People say "휴가를 내다, 휴가를 쓰다, 휴가를 받다": "내일 휴가를 내고 싶습니다."
달력의 빨간 날이 "공휴일"입니다. 설날과 추석은 사흘씩 쉽니다.
The red days on the calendar are "공휴일" (public holidays). For Seollal and Chuseok, you get three days off each.
"휴게실"(break room), "휴게 시간"(break time)의 "휴게"도 같은 "휴"입니다.
The "휴게" in "휴게실" (break room) and "휴게 시간" (break time) is the same "휴".
dl: 과장님, 다음 달에 휴가를 쓰고 싶습니다.
Manager, I'd like to take some time off next month.
gwajangnim, da-eum dare hyugareul sseugo sipseumnida
Five days. Do I have annual leave left?
You have seven days left. Hand in the request form.
sm: 정해진 날은 "휴일", 신청하는 날은 "휴가", 잠깐은 "휴식"입니다.
Fixed days are "휴일", days you ask for are "휴가", and a short break is "휴식".
qz: "I'd like to ask for time off"을 한국어로?
일하다가 십 분 쉬는 것은? 휴식 / 휴가

i: 모두 영어 "customer, guest"와 가깝습니다. 가게와 집에 온 사람은 "손님", 회사가 상대하는 사람은 "고객", 거래하는 회사는 "거래처"입니다.
All are close to "customer, guest" in English. People who come to a shop or a home are "손님", people a company serves are "고객", and a company you do business with is "거래처".
w: There are a lot of customers today.
When guests come, greet them first.
How may I help you? (to a customer)
고객 센터에 전화하면 통역을 해 줘요.
gogaek senteo-e jeonhwahamyeon tongyeogeul hae jwoyo
If you call the customer center, they will interpret for you.
Someone from our client company visited.
I sent a price quote to our client.
Pack the items for our client first.
I'm a regular at this restaurant.
단골 가게 사장님이 영어를 조금 해요.
dan-gol gage sajangnimi yeongeoreul jogeum haeyo
The owner of my regular shop speaks a little English.
Visitors, please register on the first floor.
There are a lot of visitors today.
Visitors, please borrow a safety helmet.
An order came in from our client.
I'd like to cancel my order.
Orders have piled up, so we're busy this week.
tp: 부를 때는 "손님", "고객님"이라고 합니다. "손님님"이라고 하지 않습니다. "손님"에 이미 "님"이 들어 있습니다.
When you call someone, say "손님" or "고객님". Don't say "손님님". "손님" already has "님" in it.
싱가포르의 한국 회사 사무실에서는 "거래처"와 "고객사"를 자주 듣습니다. 전화를 받으면 회사 이름과 이름을 꼭 적습니다.
In the offices of Korean companies in Singapore, you often hear "거래처" and "고객사". When you answer the phone, always write down the company name and the person's name.
dl: Manager, a guest from our client company is here.
It's General Manager Park from Seoul Trading. I showed him to the meeting room.
Thank you. Please get some tea ready.
sm: 가게와 집은 "손님", 회사와 은행은 "고객", 거래하는 회사는 "거래처"입니다.
Shops and homes have "손님", companies and banks have "고객", and a company you do business with is "거래처".

i: 일하는 곳을 가리키는 말입니다. 영어 "company, factory, site, workplace"입니다.
Words for places of work: "company, factory, site, workplace".
w: I go to work by bus.
Write down the company address in Korean.
to keep (사 두다 = to buy and keep)
We make parts at the factory.
The factory runs 24 hours a day.
Wear a safety helmet on site.
The site is far, so I leave early.
Please send me the location of the site on a map.
I'd like to change my workplace.
Please tell me the address of the workplace.
If the workplace address changes, you must report it.
If you have a hard time at work, get counseling.
The office is on the second floor.
Pay slips are handed out at the office.
The head office is in Seoul.
Someone came from the head office.
The head office came for a safety inspection.
to come out, to come in (to work)
x: 회사에 다니다 = to work at a company
tp: "사업장"은 법과 서류의 말입니다. 일터를 옮기는 것을 서류에서는 "사업장 변경"이라고 합니다.
"사업장" is a word used in law and documents. Moving to another workplace is called "사업장 변경" in official papers.
"현장"은 일이 실제로 벌어지는 곳입니다. 공사 현장, 생산 현장, 사고 현장. "현장 직원"은 사무실이 아닌 곳에서 일하는 사람입니다.
"현장" is where the work actually happens: 공사 현장 (construction site), 생산 현장 (production floor), 사고 현장 (accident scene). "현장 직원" are people who work outside the office.
dl: Which workplace are you working at now?
I work at the Hanguk Electronics factory in Jeonju.
Do you work in the office or on site?
I work on the production floor.
sm: 넓게는 "회사", 만드는 곳은 "공장", 일이 벌어지는 곳은 "현장", 서류에서는 "사업장"입니다.
In general use "회사", for a place that makes things "공장", for where work happens "현장", and in documents "사업장".
qz: 일터를 옮기는 것을 서류에서 무엇이라고 합니까?

i: 말할 때 쓰는 고유어와 서류에 쓰는 한자어가 짝을 이룹니다. 뜻은 같고 말씨가 다릅니다.
Native Korean words used in speech pair up with Chinese-origin words used in documents. They mean the same but differ in style.
w: 이 서류에 틀린 이름을 고쳐 주세요.
i seoryu-e teullin ireumeul gocheo juseyo
Please correct the wrong name on this document.
It takes two days to repair.
How much does it cost to repair a phone screen?
방을 일 층으로 바꿀 수 있어요?
bangeul il cheungeuro bakkul su isseoyo?
Can I change to a room on the first floor?
The fluorescent light is flickering, so please replace it.
Please exchange it for another size.
You can exchange it if you have the receipt.
It's too small, so I'd like to exchange it for a bigger size.
We check the fire extinguishers every month.
If something is wrong, report it right away.
I reported the accident to the team leader.
Be sure to report even small accidents.
tp: 안내판은 한자어로 되어 있습니다. "수리 중"(under repair), "점검 중"(under inspection), "사용 금지"(do not use), "교체 필요"(needs replacing).
Signs use Chinese-origin words: "수리 중" (under repair), "점검 중" (under inspection), "사용 금지" (do not use), "교체 필요" (needs replacing).
"교체"는 낡은 것을 새것으로 가는 것이고, "교환"은 서로 맞바꾸는 것입니다. 가게에서는 "교환, 환불"입니다.
"교체" means replacing an old thing with a new one, and "교환" means swapping one thing for another. In shops, you see "교환, 환불" (exchange, refund).
dl: 반장님, 이 기계에서 이상한 소리가 납니다.
Team leader, this machine is making a strange noise.
banjangnim, i gige-eseo isanghan soriga namnida
Stop it right away. Let's check it.
벨트가 낡은 것 같습니다. 바꿔야 합니까?
I think the belt is worn out. Do we need to change it?
belteuga nalgeun geot gatseumnida bakkwoya hamnikka?
네, 교체해야겠어요. "수리 중" 표시를 붙여 놓아요.
Yes, we'll have to replace it. Put up an "Under repair" sign.
ne, gyochehaeyagesseoyo "suri jung" pyosireul butyeo noayo
sm: 말로는 "고치다, 바꾸다", 서류와 안내판은 "수리, 교체, 점검"입니다.
In speech use "고치다, 바꾸다"; in documents and on signs use "수리, 교체, 점검".
qz: 가게에서 다른 것으로 바꾸는 것은? 교체 / 교환

i: 일이 끝나는 것을 나타내는 말입니다. 저절로 끝나면 "끝나다", 내가 끝맺으면 "마치다, 끝내다", 서류에서는 "완료하다"입니다.
Words for finishing work. If it ends by itself, use "끝나다"; if you finish it, "마치다, 끝내다"; in documents, "완료하다".
w: Talk about renewing your contract before your employment contract ends.
Finish the work quickly and take a rest.
Finish the cleaning too before you leave work.
Let me know when you finish the work.
When you finish the training, you get a certificate.
When the money transfer is complete, you get a text.
What time do you leave work?
오늘은 잔업 없이 여섯 시에 퇴근해요.
oneureun janeop eopsi yeoseot sie toegeunhaeyo
Today there's no overtime, so I leave work at six.
비자 연장 신청 마감이 다음 주예요.

On screens or documents, "완료" means "completed", "진행 중" means "in progress", and "예정" means "scheduled".
"끝"은 명사입니다. "이제 끝이에요"(It's over now), "끝까지 하세요"(Do it to the end).
"끝" is a noun: "이제 끝이에요" (It's over now), "끝까지 하세요" (Do it to the end).
